title: Concrete Short Cap 1-2 Pole
description: Concrete Poles with a 1-2 Alternating Sidearm configuration and a short cap which lies directly on top of the pole are most commonly found in Eastern Cordoba

title: Concrete Up-Facing Insulators 1-2 Pole
description: Poles with a 1-2 sidearm configuration and insulators which stand on top of the sidearms are a good clue to regionguess the eastern plains as they are almost non-existent in Buenos Aires with the exception of a small region on the South coast of the state

title: Concrete Long Cap 1-2 Pole
description: This pole type can be recognized by the top extension being longer than the section between the two sidearms while also having a cap on top of the extension. It is quite rare, however 90+% of the mapped specimen of this type are found in the states of Santiago del Estero and Tucuman - there is a chance they do exist elsewhere too due to its low appearance numbers.

title: Concrete Alternating Sidearm No Cap Pole
description: This type with 3 alternating sidearms with down-facing insulators at the end and an extension of varying lengths at the top of the pole with no cap is by far most commonly found in Cordoba, but is also decently common in Jujuy and Salta as well a Buenos Aires (especially in the South).

title: Concrete Single Crossbar Even Config Pole
description: This pole type with 2 or 3 insulators evenly spread out over a single crossbar can be found scattered across almost the entire country, however is notably more common in the North-West as well as San Luis, Cordoba and Buenos Aires while being rare in the Central Northern states.

title: Metal Fork Poletop No/Short Extension
description: This pole type - characterized by its poletop with insulators hanging from diagonal setup of 2-3 metal bars which can be found on both wooden and concrete poles - in the version where the pole barely goes beyond the intersection with the highest metal bar is by far most commonly found in Corrientes (+ Misiones spill), however does also exist somewhat frequently in Buenos Aires and possibly some of the Western states. This pole is mainly useful to distinguish Corrientes from neighbouring states to the West and South.

title: Metal Fork Poletop Medium Extension
description: This pole type - characterized by its poletop with insulators hanging from a diagonal setup of 2-3 metal bars which can be found on both wooden and concrete poles - in its version where the pole extends a bit above the intersection with the highest metal bar can most commonly be found in San Luis and Misiones as well as Eastern Rio Negro and Chubut and on a few roads around La Rioja.

title: Metal Fork Poletop Long Extension
description: This pole type - characterized by its poletop with insulators hanging from a diagonal setup of 2-3 metal bars which can be found on both wooden and concrete poles - in its version where the pole extends far beyond the intersection with the highest metal bar can most commonly be found in Misiones and Jujuy and more rarely in Corrientes and other North-Western States.

title: Mendoza Drainage
description: These open-air drainage ditches or canals can be seen along the streets throughout the province of Mendoza—a unique feature of the region that can be very useful in an urban loc.

title: Red chevrons with the arrow not touching the sides
description: The most useful variant of the standard red-on-white chevron: the red arrow does NOT touch the sides of the sign. Found in Salta, San Juan, southern Santa Cruz, on the RN7 and, above all, in eastern Buenos Aires. The design differs slightly from province to province.

title: Arrow-not-touching chevrons on a divided highway: eastern Buenos Aires
description: If you see the red chevron whose arrow does not touch the sides of the sign on a divided highway, you are in eastern Buenos Aires (RN2, RP11, RP63, RP56). Really useful!

title: 'Flag' and 'squashed' chevrons (Entre Ríos)
description: The 'flag' design, with the chevron to one side of the sign (1), and the 'squashed' design, slightly wider than the chevron is tall (2), are mainly found in Entre Ríos. Sometimes a chevron has both features.

title: Newer 'flag' chevrons on the RN3 (Bahía Blanca–Viedma)
description: This exact variation of the flag chevron is found on the RN3 between Bahía Blanca and Viedma. It looks newer than the Entre Ríos one: the chevron itself looks 'normal', unlike the slightly odd, older-looking Entre Ríos design.

title: White-on-blue chevrons (Córdoba)
description: The well-known white-on-blue chevrons of Córdoba province. They are not really present in the southern third of the province, for lack of bends. Classic red-on-white chevrons can still be found on non-divided national roads.

title: Blue-on-white chevrons on divided highways
description: This blue-on-white chevron (the one in Zi8gzag's video) is found on divided highways: RN7, RN8, RN9, RN14, RN34, RN38 and Autopista Presidente Perón. Regular signs can still be found on those roads.

title: Black-on-yellow chevrons (Mendoza, Neuquén)
description: Black-on-yellow chevrons can randomly be found throughout the country, but mainly in Mendoza and Neuquén.

title: Fluorescent black-on-yellow chevrons (Mendoza)
description: The fluorescent design of the black-on-yellow chevron (lighter, reflective yellow) is only found in Mendoza.

title: Yellow-on-black chevrons (Jujuy, Entre Ríos, Mendoza)
description: Yellow-on-black chevrons can randomly be found throughout the country, but mainly in Jujuy, Entre Ríos and Mendoza.

title: Fluorescent yellow-on-black chevrons (Jujuy)
description: The fluorescent design of the yellow-on-black chevron is only found in Jujuy.

title: Yellow-on-black 'flag' chevrons (Entre Ríos)
description: The 'flag' design of the yellow-on-black chevron, with the chevron to one side, is only found in Entre Ríos.

title: Arrow signs with or without chevrons (Neuquén, Córdoba, Salta, Jujuy)
description: Signs with arrows, sometimes along with classic chevrons, come in many variants. Still rare overall, but more common in Neuquén, Córdoba, Salta and Jujuy.

title: Unusual T-intersection signs (Santiago del Estero)
description: These odd T-intersection signs are only found in Santiago del Estero; the classic design can still be found on national roads (RN). One chevron in the same style was also found there.

title: Road number on the sign, between the arrows (La Pampa)
description: T-intersection signs with the road NUMBER on the sign, BETWEEN the arrows, are occasionally found in La Pampa (being replaced by the classic style, so really rare in Gen 4). Not to be confused with signs carrying the number BELOW the arrows, usually on a separate sign, which are found everywhere — or with the rare national roads that have their number on the sign.

title: Square stone bollards
description: Square bollards, always made of stone, painted or not, are useful for 50/50s: they are absent or really rare in Buenos Aires, Chaco, Formosa, Córdoba, La Pampa, Santa Cruz, Chubut and Tierra del Fuego.

title: Spanish-style bollards
description: Spanish-style bollards are found in Neuquén Province, on the RN9 in Jujuy and on the RN7 west of Mendoza. They can very occasionally be seen elsewhere.

title: Italian-style bollards (Santa Cruz)
description: Italian-style bollards are found in Santa Cruz (one was seen in Río Negro, so they are possible elsewhere, very rarely).

title: Small blue bollards north of La Rioja city
description: This little blue bollard is only found north of the city of La Rioja. The black variant is rarer.

title: Snow poles on the RN231 (Villa La Angostura)
description: Only four roads in Argentina have proper snow poles. The RN231 near Villa La Angostura (Neuquén) has this very distinct design.

title: Snow poles on the RP26 to Caviahue
description: Only four roads in Argentina have proper snow poles. This design is found on the RP26 to Caviahue, in Neuquén.

title: Snow poles on the RN7 and the RP222 to Las Leñas (Mendoza)
description: Only four roads in Argentina have proper snow poles. This design is found on both the RN7 (west of Punta de Vacas) and the RP222 to Las Leñas, in Mendoza.

title: RN7 snow pole variant (Mendoza)
description: On the RN7 west of Punta de Vacas you can also find this variant of snow pole.

title: Round symbol on signs (Buenos Aires)
description: Some signs and chevrons in Buenos Aires have this round symbol (top right of the chevron). It is very rare, though.

title: 'Santa Fe' written on road signs
description: Some signs in Santa Fe have 'Santa Fe' written on them along with the road number (here 'DPV-STA.FE-RP15', at the junction of the RP15 and RP93). It is really small and not always readable, but Santa Fe is the only province doing this.
